picks.excerpt: A record eight Pulitzer winners and finalists disclosed AI use in their 2026 submissions, and administrator Marjorie Miller says future book entry forms will carry an AI-disclosure question. The same roundup has HarperCollins saying AI will expand audiobook voices and sound effects and drive its international translation programme.
picks.rationale: The most prestigious prize in American letters is about to put an AI-disclosure box on its book entry form — that turns disclosure from etiquette into a submission requirement authors and editors have to answer.

picks.excerpt: COPE's new Code of Conduct and Core Principles deliberately contain no AI-specific clauses: Ridgway says AI tools and AI-detection tools are changing so fast that named references 'would risk being outdated by the time it was published.' Instead publishers are told to handle AI through general ethics principles and their own house policies.
picks.rationale: Publishing ethics' reference standard just decided NOT to name AI — which pushes the burden of writing an AI policy back onto every individual publisher and editor, starting now.

picks.excerpt: After a 24-hour AI writing challenge the hosts found their default model order was backwards: run cheap models for ideation, outlining and bulk drafting, then spend premium tokens only on final prose passes. A cost-and-quality routing pattern for book-length AI workflows.
picks.rationale: A concrete model-routing rule anyone drafting a book with AI can apply tomorrow — cheap models up front, premium tokens only on the prose pass — with a measured cost and quality payoff.

picks.excerpt: Novelcrafter benchmarks Opus 5 against its predecessors and its Sonnet and Fable siblings on actual fiction drafting, weighing the price jump against prose quality. A practical model-selection guide for novelists running AI inside a story-bible workflow.
picks.rationale: A hands-on Opus 5 benchmark on real fiction drafting inside a story-bible tool — it answers the 'is the price jump worth it' question writers are asking this week.

picks.excerpt: At a book fair a chapter that was 95% AI-written drew one question from a major imprint's buyers: how did you get it this good? Not whether it was AI — a concrete data point on how acquisition conversations are shifting from provenance to craft outcome.
picks.rationale: A first-hand acquisition-side data point that reframes the week's provenance panic: the buyer asked about craft, not about the tool — useful counterweight to the disclosure stories above.
